Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

dominate verb

also domination, dominant, be dominant, predominate, prevail, take over (dominate)

classical

Verg. G. 1.154: sterilēs dominantur avēnae (Lewis & Short)
Vulg. Prov. 16.32: quī dominātur animō suō

dominor, dominārī, dominātus sum

verb, first conjugation, deponent; in + abl. or inter + acc. · Conjugation on Wiktionary

be master, rule; of things, prevail, take over

From dominus: to be lord and master. Of things it means to prevail, to take over a place, as weeds a field or a passion the mind. Of people it often has the overtone of tyranny, as dominātiō does (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • rēgnō, rēgnāre, rēgnāvī, rēgnātum — reign; figuratively, have the mastery, predominate

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Or. 128: in quō ūnō rēgnat ōrātiō (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    In this sense the thing that dominates is the subject: rēgnat ōrātiō, the speech holds sway.

  • plūrimum posse — have the most power or influence; be the dominant one

    verb phrase: possum, posse, potuī; apud + acc. · also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 4: quī apud mē … plūrimum possunt (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • inter nitentia culta īnfēlīx lolium et sterilēs dominantur avēnae

    among the gleaming crops the wretched darnel and barren wild oats take overVerg. G. 1.153–154 (Lewis & Short)

  • Melior est patiēns virō fortī, et quī dominātur animō suō expugnātōre urbium.

    Better is the patient man than the strong, and he who rules his own spirit than one who takes cities.Vulg. Prov. 16.32

See also rule, control, control.
